examples.en: I went to a game room with my friends on the weekend.
The game room is crowded even at night.
A lot of game rooms have disappeared from the neighborhood lately.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나서 게임방에서 세 시간이나 놀았어요.
examples.en: The exam was over, so I played at the game room for three whole hours.
We decided to meet in front of the game room.
I'm worried because my child goes to the game room often.

explain: 요즘은 '피시방(PC방)'이라는 말을 더 많이 써요. '게임방'은 조금 예전 느낌이 나지만 무슨 뜻인지는 모두 알아요.
explain_en: These days people more often say '피시방' (PC bang). '게임방' sounds a bit old-fashioned, but everyone still understands it.

examples.en: The winter wind was so biting that my ears turned red.
I walked for a long time in the winter wind.

examples.ko: 오늘은 겨울바람 때문에 더 춥게 느껴져요.
examples.en: It feels even colder today because of the winter wind.

examples.ko: 겨울바람이 불면 따뜻한 국물이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: When the winter wind blows, I crave something with warm broth.
I packed a scarf and gloves to stand up to the winter wind.

examples.ko: 창문 틈으로 겨울바람이 들어와서 방이 추워요.
examples.en: Winter wind comes in through the gap in the window, so the room is cold.

explain: 바람이 '불다', 바람을 '맞다'와 자주 같이 써요. 같은 느낌으로 '찬바람'이라고도 하는데, 이건 겨울이 아니어도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It pairs naturally with 바람이 불다 (the wind blows) and 바람을 맞다 (to be hit by wind). '찬바람' (cold wind) is similar but can be used outside winter too.

examples.en: I need to take out the winter blanket.

examples.ko: 이 장갑은 겨울용이라서 봄에는 못 써요.
examples.en: These gloves are for winter, so I can't use them in spring.
I went to the department store to buy winter shoes.
Did you switch to winter tires?

examples.ko: 이건 겨울용이 아니라서 많이 추울 거예요.
examples.en: This isn't made for winter, so you'll probably be very cold.

examples.ko: 겨울용 옷은 부피가 커서 보관하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Winter clothes are bulky, so they're hard to store.

explain: '겨울용 + 물건'처럼 뒤에 물건 이름을 붙이거나 '겨울용이에요'로 끝낼 수 있어요. 짝이 되는 말은 '여름용'이에요.
explain_en: You can put a noun after it, like '겨울용 + item', or end a sentence with '겨울용이에요'. Its counterpart is '여름용' (for summer use).

examples.ko: 겨울잠을 자는 개구리는 땅속에서 봄을 기다려요.
examples.en: Frogs that hibernate wait for spring underground.
Snakes also hibernate when winter comes.

examples.ko: 곰은 겨울잠에 들어가기 전에 많이 먹어요.
examples.en: Bears eat a lot before they go into hibernation.

examples.ko: 겨울잠 자는 동물은 어떤 게 있어요?
examples.en: What kinds of animals hibernate?

examples.ko: 겨울잠에서 깬 곰은 배가 많이 고플 거예요.
examples.en: A bear that has woken from hibernation must be very hungry.

examples.ko: 저도 겨울잠을 자고 싶을 만큼 겨울에는 졸려요.
examples.en: I get so sleepy in winter that I feel like hibernating too.

explain: '겨울잠을 자다'가 기본 표현이에요. 사람이 겨울에 너무 졸리거나 집에만 있을 때 농담으로 '겨울잠 자고 싶다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: The basic expression is '겨울잠을 자다'. People also joke '겨울잠 자고 싶다' when they feel very sleepy or stay home all winter.

en: be absent from work; call in sick

examples.ko: 연락 없이 결근한 탓에 팀장님께 꾸중을 들었어요.
examples.en: I got scolded by my team leader because I was absent without notice.

examples.ko: 감기가 심해서 오늘은 결근을 해야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: My cold is bad, so I think I have to take today off work.
Why were you absent from work yesterday?

examples.ko: 이번 달에 한 번도 결근하지 않았어요.
examples.en: I haven't missed a single day of work this month.
If you miss work because you're sick, you need to call ahead.
That employee is often absent, so I'm worried.

explain: 회사에 와야 하는데 오지 않는 것에 써요. 학교에 안 가는 것은 '결석하다'라고 해요. 허락받고 쉬는 것은 보통 '휴가를 내다', '연차를 쓰다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when you are supposed to be at work but do not show up. Missing school is '결석하다'. Taking approved time off is usually '휴가를 내다' or '연차를 쓰다'.

examples.en: On the subway, you should leave the seniors' seats for elderly people.

examples.ko: 빈 경로석이 있어도 젊은 사람은 앉기 불편해요.
examples.en: Even when a priority seat is empty, young people feel uneasy sitting there.

examples.ko: 경로석에 앉아 계신 할머니께 말을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I spoke to the grandmother sitting in the priority seat.
You shouldn't mix up the pregnant women's seat and the seniors' seat.
There are separate seniors' seats at the front of the bus.

examples.ko: 아버지는 경로석 표시가 있는 자리를 늘 비워 두세요.
examples.en: My father always leaves the seats marked for seniors empty.

explain: 어르신이 앉도록 정해 둔 자리예요. 지하철에서는 '노약자석'이라는 말도 많이 써요. 임산부석과는 다른 자리예요.
explain_en: It is a seat reserved for elderly people. On the subway, '노약자석' is also a common name. It is separate from the seat for pregnant women.

examples.en: My older brother is so good that I feel a sense of rivalry.

examples.ko: 아이들은 놀다가 경쟁심 때문에 싸우기도 해요.
examples.en: Kids sometimes fight over competitiveness while playing.
A moderate amount of competitiveness helps with studying.

examples.ko: 친구에게 경쟁심을 느끼는 건 나쁜 일이 아니에요.
examples.en: Feeling competitive toward a friend is not a bad thing.

examples.ko: 그 둘은 경쟁심이 강해서 늘 내기를 해요.
examples.en: Those two are so competitive that they always make bets.
Burning with the urge to compete, I practiced all night.

explain: '경쟁심이 강하다/생기다/들다'처럼 써요. '승부욕'은 이기고 싶은 마음이고, '경쟁심'은 상대를 의식하는 마음이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It appears in phrases like '경쟁심이 강하다/생기다/들다'. '승부욕' is the desire to win, while '경쟁심' leans more toward being conscious of a rival.

examples.en: I bought a compact car because it's easy to park.
Compact cars use less gas money.

examples.ko: 경차는 주차장 요금을 깎아 주는 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Many parking lots give a discount to compact cars.
It's a compact car, so it's hard to load big luggage.

examples.ko: 저는 큰 차보다 경차가 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like compact cars more than big cars.

examples.ko: 경차 한 대로 온 가족이 여행을 갔어요.
examples.en: The whole family went on a trip in one compact car.

explain: '경차'는 '가벼운 차'가 아니라 배기량 등 기준에 맞는 작은 차를 부르는 말이에요. '소형차'와 비슷하지만 경차가 더 작고, 세금이나 요금 혜택이 있는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: '경차' is a legal-style category for small cars (by engine size and so on), not just any light car. It is similar to '소형차' (small car), but smaller, and it often comes with tax or fee benefits.

examples.en: In winter, you can smell egg bread on the street.
On my way home from work, I bought and ate warm egg bread.
Egg bread is sweet and salty, so it's delicious.
How much is one egg bread?
The child dropped some on his clothes while eating egg bread.
This shop's egg bread is the tastiest.

explain: 빵 반죽 안에 계란이 통째로 들어간 길거리 간식이에요. '달걀빵'이라고도 해요. 한국에서는 '계란'과 '달걀'을 둘 다 써요.
explain_en: It is a street snack with a whole egg baked inside sweet bread batter. It is also called '달걀빵'. Korean uses both '계란' and '달걀' for egg.

examples.en: You need continual effort for your skills to improve.
It keeps raining, so the roads are jammed.
The company promised continued support.
You have to study Korean continuously so you don't forget it.

examples.ko: 공사 소음이 계속적이라서 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: The construction noise is nonstop, so I can't sleep.
Thank you for your continued interest.

explain: 말할 때는 그냥 '계속'이나 '계속해서'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '계속적'은 글이나 발표, 인사말처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 어울려요. 보통 '계속적인', '계속적으로' 꼴로 써요.
explain_en: In casual speech, plain '계속' or '계속해서' sounds much more natural. '계속적' fits writing, presentations and formal greetings. It usually appears as '계속적인' or '계속적으로'.

en: class for advanced learners; the highest-level class

examples.en: Next semester I'll study in the advanced class.
The advanced class has a lot of discussion.
I did well on the test and moved up to the advanced class.

examples.ko: 고급반에 들어가려면 레벨 테스트를 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To get into the advanced class, you have to take a level test.
The friends in the advanced class speak Korean really well.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 고급반이 아니라서 신문 기사가 어려워요.
examples.en: I'm not in the advanced class yet, so news articles are hard for me.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '초급반', '중급반'이에요. 학원이나 어학당 수업을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: Its companions are '초급반' (beginner class) and '중급반' (intermediate class). It is often used for classes at academies and language institutes.

examples.en: I took a lump of meat out of the fridge.
First slice the big lump of meat thinly.
There are big chunks of meat in the soup.
The longer you boil a chunk of meat, the softer it gets.
Don't eat only the meat; have some vegetables too.
I bought a geun of meat in one piece at the market.

explain: 썰지 않은 큰 고기 한 덩이를 말해요. 이미 썰어 놓은 고기 조각은 '고기 조각'이나 '고기 한 점'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a big piece of meat that has not been sliced. Pieces that are already cut are called '고기 조각' or '고기 한 점'.

examples.en: The child blew up a balloon and it popped.
The balloon floated away into the sky.

examples.ko: 생일 파티에 고무풍선을 열 개 달았어요.
examples.en: I hung ten balloons at the birthday party.
A rubber balloon pops when it touches a needle.
I wrote a name on a balloon and gave it as a gift.
Please buy me just one balloon.

explain: 그냥 '풍선'이라고 해도 보통 같은 물건을 말해요. 불다, 터지다, 날아가다 같은 말과 같이 많이 써요.
explain_en: Just saying '풍선' usually refers to the same thing. It goes with verbs like 불다 (blow up), 터지다 (pop) and 날아가다 (fly away).

examples.ko: 해외 주재원의 자녀 교육 문제는 늘 큰 고민거리예요.
examples.en: Educating children of overseas postings is always a big worry.

examples.ko: 요즘 고민거리가 많아서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I have a lot on my mind lately, so I can't sleep.
If you have something troubling you, tell me.
Getting a job was my biggest worry.
I told my friend what was bothering me and felt better.
The child's grades became a worry for the parents.

explain: '고민거리가 생기다/있다/되다'처럼 써요. '걱정거리'와 비슷한데, 고민거리는 어떻게 할지 생각이 많은 문제에 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used as '고민거리가 생기다/있다/되다'. It is close to '걱정거리', but '고민거리' fits problems where you keep thinking about what to do.

examples.en: Gomguk gets rich only when you boil it for a long time.
My mom made me gomguk because I was sick.
Eating rice in gomguk is filling.
One bowl of gomguk, please.
When gomguk cools, the fat hardens on top.

examples.ko: 곰국 간은 먹을 때 소금으로 맞춰요.
examples.en: You season gomguk with salt when you eat it.

explain: 소고기나 뼈를 오래 끓여 하얗고 진하게 만든 국이에요. 식당 메뉴에서는 '곰탕'이라는 이름을 더 많이 봐요.
explain_en: It is a soup made by boiling beef or bones for a long time until it turns milky and rich. On restaurant menus you will more often see the name '곰탕'.

examples.en: We learned the rules of multiplication in math class.

examples.ko: 곱셈은 같은 수를 여러 번 더하는 것과 같아요.
examples.en: Multiplication is the same as adding the same number several times.
To do multiplication, you have to memorize the times tables.
Addition and subtraction are easy, but multiplication is hard.
There were ten multiplication problems.
The child put a multiplication chart on the wall.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 덧셈, 뺄셈, 나눗셈이에요. 계산할 때는 '3 곱하기 4'처럼 '곱하기'라고 읽어요.
explain_en: Its companions are 덧셈, 뺄셈 and 나눗셈. When you calculate aloud, you say '3 곱하기 4' (3 times 4).

examples.en: On cold days, I think of gopchang hot pot.
After the gopchang hot pot, we ate fried rice too.
Gopchang hot pot is tasty because the broth is spicy and hearty.
I ordered two servings of gopchang hot pot with my friends.
It tastes even better when you add glass noodles to gopchang hot pot.
I like sundae soup more than gopchang hot pot.

explain: 소의 작은창자인 곱창과 채소를 넣고 상 위에서 끓여 먹는 국물 요리예요. '찌개'보다 재료가 푸짐하고 여럿이 함께 먹는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a hot pot cooked at the table with beef small intestine (곱창) and vegetables. Compared with '찌개', it has more ingredients and feels meant to be shared.

examples.en: The kids are playing with a ball on the playground.
We broke a window while playing with a ball.
Ball games are more fun the more people there are.
Do you want to go to the park to play ball?

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 매일 골목에서 공놀이로 하루를 보냈어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I spent every day playing ball in the alley.

examples.ko: 공놀이에 푹 빠져서 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was so absorbed in the ball game that I lost track of time.

explain: 축구나 야구처럼 규칙이 있는 경기보다 공을 가지고 가볍게 노는 느낌이에요. 보통 '공놀이를 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It feels like casual play with a ball, rather than a rule-based sport such as soccer or baseball. It usually appears as '공놀이를 하다'.

examples.en: It is important to follow public etiquette.

examples.ko: 지하철에서 큰 소리로 통화하면 공중도덕에 어긋나요.
examples.en: Talking loudly on the phone on the subway goes against public manners.

examples.ko: 공중도덕은 모두가 편하게 지내기 위한 약속이에요.
examples.en: Public etiquette is an agreement so that everyone can be comfortable.

examples.ko: 공중도덕이 없는 사람 때문에 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I got angry because of someone with no manners in public.
Standing in line is also part of public etiquette.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 공중도덕 캠페인을 자주 해요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood often runs public etiquette campaigns.

explain: '공중도덕을 지키다'가 가장 자주 나오는 표현이에요. 반대로 안 지키는 사람에게는 '매너가 없다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: '공중도덕을 지키다' (to follow public etiquette) is the most common phrase. For someone who doesn't, people also say '매너가 없다' (has no manners).

examples.en: On the weekend I went to the public bathhouse with my father.
At a public bathhouse, you shower and then get into the tub.
Public bathhouses have decreased a lot these days.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 공중목욕탕에서 먹던 바나나우유가 생각나요.
examples.en: I remember the banana milk I drank at the bathhouse as a kid.

examples.ko: 공중목욕탕 가는 날은 온 가족이 일찍 일어났어요.
examples.en: On bathhouse days, the whole family woke up early.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 오래된 공중목욕탕이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is one old public bathhouse in this neighborhood.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '목욕탕'이라고 많이 말해요. 여러 사람이 함께 쓰는 곳이라 공중도덕을 지켜야 해요.
explain_en: In daily speech people often just say '목욕탕'. Many people share the space, so you need to follow public etiquette.

examples.en: In winter, we dry persimmons to make gotgam.
Have you heard the story of the tiger and the dried persimmon?
Gotgam is chewy and sweet, so kids like it.
Do you want to try just one gotgam?

examples.ko: 처마 밑에 곶감이 주렁주렁 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: Dried persimmons hang in bunches under the eaves.
Some people float gotgam in sujeonggwa to eat it.

explain: 껍질을 벗긴 감을 말려서 만든 간식이에요. 감을 말린 것이라 겨울 간식으로 많이 먹어요.

phrases.example: 저금한 돈을 곶감 꼬치에서 곶감 빼 먹듯 쓰다 보니 금세 바닥났어요.
phrases.en: I kept dipping into my savings bit by bit, and they ran out quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모아 둔 것을 아끼지 않고 하나씩 꺼내 쓰는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes using up what you saved piece by piece, without holding back.
phrases.en_equiv: to dip into one's savings bit by bit

explain_en: It is a snack made by peeling and drying persimmons. It is a popular winter snack.

examples.en: This year every fruit tree is loaded with fruit.
I planted three fruit trees in the yard.
Fruit trees bloom in spring.
Bugs got on the fruit trees, so I sprayed them.
My grandfather's farm has a lot of fruit trees.

examples.ko: 과일나무 사이로 작은 길이 나 있어요.
examples.en: A small path runs between the fruit trees.

explain: 나무를 셀 때는 '그루'를 써서 '한 그루, 두 그루'라고 해요. 사과나무, 배나무처럼 과일 이름 뒤에 '나무'를 붙이는 말도 많아요.
explain_en: Trees are counted with '그루', as in '한 그루, 두 그루'. Many specific trees are formed by adding '나무' to the fruit name, like 사과나무 and 배나무.

examples.en: The assignment is due by tomorrow.

examples.ko: 과제물이 너무 많아서 주말에도 쉬지 못해요.
examples.en: There are so many assignments that I can't rest even on weekends.
I emailed my assignment to the professor.
When is the assignment deadline?
I forgot to write my name on the assignment.
I stayed up all night yesterday because of an assignment.

explain: 초등학생이 하는 것은 보통 '숙제'라고 해요. '과제물'은 대학이나 수업에서 내는 보고서나 결과물에 더 잘 어울려요. 줄여서 '과제'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: For younger students, '숙제' is the usual word. '과제물' suits reports and work handed in for college or other classes. People often shorten it to '과제'.

examples.en: Many people on Jeju Island make a living from tourism.

examples.ko: 관광업은 날씨와 경제 상황에 영향을 많이 받아요.
examples.en: The tourism industry is greatly affected by weather and the economy.

examples.ko: 관광객이 늘면서 관광업이 다시 살아나고 있어요.
examples.en: As tourists increase, the tourism industry is recovering.
I studied the tourism industry in college.
To work in tourism, it helps to be good at foreign languages.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 관광업 덕분에 다시 활기가 생겼어요.
examples.en: This village regained its energy thanks to tourism.

explain: '관광'은 구경하며 여행하는 것이고, '관광업'은 그걸로 돈을 버는 산업이에요. 같은 '-업' 말로 '농업', '서비스업'이 있어요.
explain_en: '관광' is traveling to see sights, while '관광업' is the industry that earns money from it. Other '-업' words include '농업' (agriculture) and '서비스업' (service industry).

examples.en: I received a movie ticket as a gift.
Please show your ticket at the entrance.
I have one museum ticket left.
How much is one ticket?

examples.ko: 친구가 공연 관람권을 두 장 보내 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend sent me two tickets to a show.

examples.ko: 이 관람권으로 전시를 두 번 볼 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can I see the exhibition twice with this ticket?

explain: 영화나 전시, 공연을 보러 들어갈 수 있는 표예요. '영화 관람권'처럼 선물이나 쿠폰으로 받는 표에 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '표'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a ticket that lets you in to see a movie, exhibition or show. It is often used for gifted or coupon-style tickets, like '영화 관람권'. In daily talk people also just say '표'.

examples.en: The management office takes noise complaints in the apartment complex.

examples.ko: 형광등 교체는 관리실에 요청하면 해 줘요.
examples.en: If you ask the management office, they will replace the light tube.
I asked the man at the management office for the key.
Until what time is the management office open?
The elevator broke down, so I called the management office.

examples.ko: 관리실은 일 층 현관 옆에 있어요.
examples.en: The management office is on the first floor next to the entrance.

explain: 아파트나 건물을 관리하는 사무실이에요. 정식 이름은 '관리사무소'이고, 입구를 지키는 '경비실'과는 달라요.
explain_en: It is the office that looks after an apartment complex or building. The formal name is '관리사무소', and it differs from the '경비실' (guard booth) at the entrance.

en: advertising expense; advertising cost; advertising fee

examples.en: This month only the advertising cost went up a lot.
A new product came out, so we spent a lot on advertising.
We postponed making the video because the ad budget fell short.
Small shops feel the burden of advertising costs heavily.
How much did advertising cost this month?
The effect is small compared to the advertising cost.

explain: '광고비를 쓰다/들이다/아끼다'처럼 써요. 같은 '-비' 말로 '교통비', '식비'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is used as '광고비를 쓰다/들이다/아끼다'. Other '-비' (cost) words include '교통비' and '식비'.

examples.ko: 저는 교장실에 가 본 적이 한 번도 없어요.
examples.en: I have never been to the principal's office.

examples.ko: 교장실은 이 층 복도 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The principal's office is at the end of the second-floor hallway.
The teacher took the documents to the principal's office.

examples.ko: 교장실 앞에서 떨려서 한참 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was nervous and stood in front of the principal's office for a long time.
Where is the principal's office?

examples.ko: 상을 받은 날 교장실에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: On the day I won the prize, we took a photo in the principal's office.

explain: 학교 교장 선생님의 방이에요. 선생님들이 모여 있는 곳은 '교무실'이라서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.
explain_en: It is the room of the school principal. It is easy to confuse with '교무실', the staff room where teachers gather.

examples.en: The heel of my shoe was worn, so I left it at the shoe repair shop.

examples.ko: 구둣방 아저씨가 구두를 새것처럼 닦아 주셨어요.
examples.en: The man at the shoe repair shop polished my shoes like new.
The shoe repair shop is near the subway station.
Shoe repair shops have mostly disappeared these days.
The shoe repair shop also repairs bags.
It rained on the way to the shoe repair shop.

explain: 구두를 고치고 닦아 주는 작은 가게예요. '구두 수선집'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is a small shop that repairs and shines shoes. People also call it a '구두 수선집'.

examples.en: The road curves to the right.
The wire bent easily.
If your back is bent, it can hurt.
It's an old nail, so it bends easily.

examples.ko: 구부러진 길을 따라 걸으면 바다가 나와요.
examples.en: If you walk along the curved road, you reach the sea.
As she grew older, my grandmother's back became bent.

explain: 물건이나 길이 저절로 휘어 있는 상태를 말해요. 사람이 일부러 구부릴 때는 '구부리다'를 써서 '무릎을 구부리다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a thing or road that is bent on its own. When a person bends something on purpose, use '구부리다', as in '무릎을 구부리다' (bend one's knees).

examples.en: If you pass the national exam, you get a license.
To become a nurse, you have to take a national exam.
I practically live in the library preparing for the national exam.
On the day of the national exam, I was nervous from the morning.
When the national exam is over, I'm going on a trip.
The national exam results come out next week.

explain: 의사, 간호사, 변호사처럼 나라에서 자격을 주는 시험을 말해요. 보통 '국가시험을 보다/치르다', '국가시험에 합격하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It refers to exams that grant a state-recognized qualification, as for doctors, nurses or lawyers. It is typically used as '국가시험을 보다/치르다' or '국가시험에 합격하다'.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 긴 국경선을 맞대고 있어요.
examples.en: The two countries share a long border.
Villages near the border are quiet.

examples.ko: 국경선을 넘을 때 여권을 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to show your passport when crossing the border.
On the map, the border is drawn as a dotted line.
The border runs along the river.
There is a checkpoint at the border.

explain: 그냥 '국경'이라고도 많이 말해요. '국경을 넘다'는 자주 쓰는 표현이고, 지도의 선을 말할 때 '국경선'이 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: People also often just say '국경'. '국경을 넘다' (cross the border) is a common phrase, while '국경선' fits when talking about the line on a map.

examples.en: I filled the soup bowl to the brim with soup.
The soup bowl is hot, so be careful.
The soup bowl goes to the right of the rice bowl.
Please put the soup bowls on the table.
Please take out just two soup bowls.
I put the leftover soup in the fridge, bowl and all.

explain: 밥그릇과 국그릇이 한 상의 기본 짝이에요. 국이 아니라 찌개나 라면을 담는 그릇은 보통 '그릇'이나 '냄비'라고 말해요.
explain_en: The rice bowl and soup bowl are the basic pair on a Korean table. For stew or ramyeon, people usually just say '그릇' or '냄비'.

examples.en: My younger sibling attends a national university.
National universities tend to have lower tuition than private ones.
A professor from a national university came to give a special lecture.

examples.ko: 우리 지역 국립대가 새 캠퍼스를 열었어요.
examples.en: Our region's national university opened a new campus.

examples.ko: 국립대와 사립대 중 어디가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which is better, a national or a private university?
I graduated from a national university and work in my hometown.

explain: '국립대학교'를 줄인 말이에요. 반대되는 말은 '사립대'예요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '국립대학교'. Its opposite is '사립대' (private university).

examples.en: On Memorial Day I visited the national cemetery.
The national cemetery is a quiet and solemn place.
Many people visit the national cemetery every year.
We went on a school field trip to the national cemetery.
I took off my hat in front of the national cemetery.
The national cemetery is not far from my house.

explain: 나라를 위해 일한 분들을 모신 곳이에요. '현충원'이라는 이름으로도 많이 불러요. 장소 이름이라 조용히 하고 예의를 지켜야 해요.
explain_en: It is a place that honors people who served the nation. It is also commonly called '현충원'. Since it is a solemn site, visitors should be quiet and respectful.

examples.en: An international conference will be held in Seoul next month.
I took a plane to attend an international conference.
Interpreters are essential at international conferences.
I'm very busy these days preparing for the international conference.

examples.ko: 회사는 올해 국제회의를 두 번 주최했어요.
examples.en: The company hosted an international conference twice this year.
I translated the materials for the international conference into English.

explain: '국제회의가 열리다', '국제회의를 개최하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스나 업무에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used as '국제회의가 열리다' or '국제회의를 개최하다'. It appears more in the news and at work than in everyday chat.

examples.en: The baked sweet potato tasted so nutty that I ate one more.

examples.ko: 겨울 저녁에는 군고구마 냄새가 골목에 퍼져요.
examples.en: On winter evenings, the smell of baked sweet potatoes spreads through the alley.
Baked sweet potatoes are tastiest when eaten warm.
I bought two baked sweet potatoes on the street.
I eat baked sweet potato with dongchimi (radish water kimchi) on the side.
I tried making baked sweet potatoes in the oven.

explain: 겨울에 먹는 대표적인 간식이에요. '구운 고구마'라고 해도 되지만 간식 이름으로는 '군고구마'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is a classic winter snack. You can say '구운 고구마' too, but '군고구마' is the usual name for the snack.

examples.en: Coins are rolling around on the floor.

examples.ko: 방 안에 빈 병이 굴러다니고 있어요.
examples.en: Empty bottles are lying around in the room.

examples.ko: 공이 방 안을 굴러다니는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear a ball rolling around the room.

examples.ko: 집에 쓰지 않는 물건이 굴러다녀서 정리했어요.
examples.en: Unused things were lying around the house, so I tidied up.

examples.ko: 책상 밑에서 연필이 굴러다니는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a pencil rolling around under the desk.

examples.ko: 이 정도 돈은 길에 굴러다니지 않아요.
examples.en: This much money isn't just lying around on the street.

explain: '굴러가다'는 한 방향으로 가는 것이고, '굴러다니다'는 여기저기로 구르는 것이에요. 물건이 아무 데나 놓여 있을 때도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '굴러가다' rolls in one direction, while '굴러다니다' rolls here and there. It is also commonly used when things are lying about carelessly.
